concepts.label: Standardized Client Exception Hierarchy (CouchbaseException and derivatives)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - this is exactly the kind of client-library property called out in the batch instructions as needing its own vocabulary (error-handling/retry behavior is a property of the client library, not of any SQL++ statement). Exceptions like ParsingFailureException or CasMismatchException are the SDK's own typed wrapper around server error codes drawn from several different services (KV, Query, Analytics, Search, View, Management), so this concept spans services rather than mapping to one.

cross_product_finding: This page is a clean confirmation of the batch instructions' expectation: error-handling/exception-hierarchy is exactly the kind of thing that 'is a property of the client library, not of any SQL++ statement' and needed its own vocabulary. Even though several exception definitions cross-reference server/'s N1QL error-code ranges (e.g. #18 IndexExists ties to the same failure server/'s CREATE INDEX page would describe), the SDK's own error TAXONOMY - the numbered ID ranges (1-99 shared, 100-199 KV, 200-299 Query, 300-399 Analytics, 400-499 Search, 500-599 View, 600-699 Management API, 700-799 Field-Level Encryption) and the CouchbaseException class hierarchy - has no counterpart anywhere in server/'s or cloud/'s statement-reference vocabulary. It is a many-to-one mapping (many server error codes across many services collapse into one typed Java exception), which is structurally unlike a 1:1 statement reuse case, so minting sdk:error-handling and sdk:query-error-mapping is the right call rather than trying to attach this page's content onto any single n1ql:* concept.
notable_absence: Did not attempt to mint or link every one of the ~50 individual numbered exceptions on this page as separate concepts - captured the taxonomy-level concepts plus one representative cross-link to server/'s N1QL error codes, since exhaustive per-exception extraction was judged out of proportion to the batch's central question.
